ai.headline: Solid elevated plank that improves as it goes, but the hips start too high and the head is lifted.
good: Elbows are locked and arms stay straight throughout the hold.
Hands are planted flat and feet are up on the toes for a stable base.
Hips lower and the body line straightens noticeably in the later frames.
The elevated position on the bench is a good way to build plank endurance.

fix.issue: Hips are piked upward, especially in frames 1 to 4, breaking the straight line from shoulders to ankles.
fix.cue: Squeeze your glutes and lower your hips until your body is a straight line.

fix.issue: The head is lifted and the neck is extended, particularly visible in frames 2 to 6.
fix.cue: Tuck your chin slightly and look at the floor to keep your neck neutral.

fix.issue: The high hips and slightly rounded back suggest the core is not fully braced.
fix.cue: Brace your abs like you're about to be poked in the stomach.

ai.over_time: The form improves during the set; the hips start high with slightly bent knees in the first few frames, then gradually lower and straighten out by the final frames.
ai.next_set: Focus on starting with your hips in line with your shoulders and ankles from the very first second.
